articleTitle: Flexible Human-Robot Interaction: Collaborative Robot Integrated with Hand Tracking
abstract: The rising demand for adaptable and user-friendly forms of interaction in the field of manufacturing and assembly tasks has led to increased attention on human-robot collaboration. Collaborative robots (cobots) have emerged as a promising solution to address this demand. In this study, we propose the integration and application of cobots along with a pre-trained deep learning model to assist users in assembly activities, specifically part handover and storage. The human-robot interaction is facilitated through a hand tracking system that enables a close approach to the user's hand. Testing on the system yielded 99% accuracy. The incorporation of deep learning models in cobot applications holds substantial potential for industry transformation, with implications spanning manufacturing, healthcare, and assistive technologies. This research serves as a compelling proof of concept, showcasing the effective implementation of deep learning models to facilitate close human-robot interactions.

articleTitle: Implementation of Potential Fields in a Differential Mobile Robot (TurtleBot2)
abstract: This paper focuses on the implementation of a method based on the physical principle of “Potential Fields.” A differential robot, known as TurtleBot2 (Kobuki), was utilized to address the problem of autonomous navigation. To perceive the environment, a laser-based object detection and measurement system was used, enabling TurtleBot2 to navigate complex environments by detecting and avoiding obstacles. Additionally, an NVIDIA Jetson Nano ARM architecture computer was utilized, equipped with a streamlined set of instructions for essential processing, enabling it to control the robot's angular and linear speed. The wireless connection between the computer and the TurtleBot2 enabled efficient information transfer and data processing. This wireless connection extends robot's working range based on Wi-Fi network coverage, ensuring safe navigation in restricted and challenging spaces. Tests were conducted in two distinct environments, presenting results from both simulation and experimentation, demonstrating the efficacy of the technique.

articleTitle: Humanoid Robot Replicated Using Biosignals

authors.preferredName: L. J. de La Cruz Martínez

abstract: This project develops the construction of a humanoid robot that will replicate the eye movement (up, down, left and right) using an Electrooculogram (EOG), which is digitally processed using Matlab software and an Electromyogram (EMG) to replicate the movement of the jaw (up and down). Through these biosignals, a set of electric servomotors adapted to a humanoid head built by additive manufacturing (3D printed) for academic use will be put into operation, showing basic principles of robotics, and biosignal processing that, through the replication of eye and mouth movements, seeks to attract the curiosity of new users to the world of robotics.

articleTitle: Automatic Row Switching Algorithm Using 2D LiDAR
abstract: Autonomous navigation in greenhouses algorithms have been developed to enhance the greenhouse productivity in order to satisfy the high demand of resource the overpopulation is causing. Many authors have already designed navigation algorithms when the robot is inside the lane; nevertheless, there are no algorithms to change lane at the headland of the greenhouse. This work uses a 2D LIDAR to develop an automatic row-switching algorithm using obstacle avoidance techniques by adding the vectors created by the LIDAR lectures and using weighted vectors to propel the robot to the other row. This algorithm was tested in a greenhouse at the end of a row, obtaining 93% of efficiency.

articleTitle: Geometric Figure Identification System Implemented in the AutoMiny 4.0 Platform, Based on Computational Vision.*
abstract: The development of new tools with the support of Artificial Intelligence (AI) models continues to progress significantly. Computational Vision, a subfield of AI, provides a mechanism that can interact with its environment by capturing and processing digital images. This paper presents the development of a system that enables the identification of geometric figures by extracting seven mathematical features using computer vision techniques. These features were used to train two Machine Learning classification models, of which one stands out for presenting a classification percentage of 99%. The model was tested in the AutoMiny 4.0 platform to provide the robot with actions based on the identification of each figure, thereby enabling its autonomy in decision-making.

articleTitle: Limit Cycle Construction Using Bézier Curves: Application in a Mobile Robot
abstract: A methodology is proposed to design a wide range of simple closed curves not parameterized by time using second-order Bézier curves. A Hamiltonian system and a gradient system are designed, which in turn produce a velocity field that points to the closed curve. The velocity field is used as a reference for a mobile robot to follow the closed curve asymptotically. Numerical and experimental results are presented, which are implemented in a low-budget experimental platform.

articleTitle: Q-Learning for Autonomous Vehicle Navigation
abstract: In this work, we proposed and developed a reinforcement Q-learning method to do the lane-keeping and obstacle evasion driving maneuvers. We detail how to design a simple car simulator and how to use it to do the training. For each problem, we define different states, actions, and reward functions to obtain a Q-table. Next, we use it as a driving maneuver controller in a different simulation environment. With this method, our car successfully droves on a road different to where it was training. An important conclusion is the possibility to build, more complex controllers to do passing or behavior selectors.

articleTitle: Simulation and Experimental Analysis of a Humanoid Robot Walking on a Sloping Surface in an Arbitrary Direction
abstract: Walking patterns for humanoid robots have been studied in the literature based on different approaches. Most of them are inspired by human walking and consider that the robot walk on a horizontal plane with symmetrical motions of the legs. Conversely, in this paper, studies are carried out to determine the values of the parameters associated with a stable walking pattern that uses cycloidal motions of the torso and the free foot, for the robot moving in any direction on an inclined plane. Such studies are based on the behavior of the ZMP in the walking. Experimental results validate the efficacy of the approach.

articleTitle: Optimal Control for the Humanoid Robots Balance
abstract: In this article, a control approach is presented to maintain the static balance in both the sagittal and the frontal plane of a humanoid robot that is modeled as a cart-table system. The main objective is to design a state feedback controller to balance of the humanoid robot even in the presence of disturbances caused by interactions with the environment or other robots. In order to evaluate the performance of this technique, various experiments were conducted on a NAO humanoid robot using a simulation software based on physics engines. Successful results were obtained for balance regulation tasks, even in the presence of external disturbances, demonstrating the effectiveness and robustness of the proposed control scheme.

articleTitle: Efficient Spatial Coordination for Multi-Robot Exploration
abstract: In this study, we introduce an efficient approach for spatial coordination in cooperative robotics using Unmanned Ground Vehicles (UGV) and Unmanned Aerial Vehicles (UAV). The approach involves distributing mathematical calculations among three roles: a central robot, an upper robot, and multiple surrounding robots. To maintain the desired parametric formation, we propose a specific control law based on the linear and angular velocity of the central robot, enabling dynamic formation adjustments for efficient exploration. Our strategy employs visual localization with ArUco markers and artificial potential fields for navigation. We present experimental results utilizing Robot Operating System (ROS) and OpenCV.

articleTitle: Intelligent Control Applied to a Mobile Robot for Recognition and Collection of Plastic Bottles
abstract: This article presents the control of a mobile robot for the recognition and collection of plastic bottles applying artificial intelligence techniques. The robot was equipped with a mechanical arm with six degrees of freedom, on which two video cameras were mounted, so that the vertical movement of the arm allows changing the orientation of the cameras. In this way, it is possible to locate nearby and distant bottles, and not lose sight of them while the robot moves towards them. To recognize the bottles, a convolutional neural network was trained. To approach the bottles and collect them, a diffuse system was designed. The results show an accuracy of 95.3% in the recognition of the bottles and 87% in the approximation and collection process, with an average time of 43 seconds.

articleTitle: Experimental Evaluation of a Force Regulation Scheme on a Planar Robot Without Force Sensors
abstract: Robot manipulators are complex systems that are frequently exposed to various sources of disturbances, such as unmodeled dynamics, varying payloads, friction, unexpected collisions, or compliant interaction forces. Perturbation observers find two common applications in the literature concerning robot manipulators: a) mitigating and rejecting these perturbations, and b) serving as force/torque (F/T) estimators in situations where an F/T sensor is unavailable for force control applications or to design cost-effective robotic systems for interaction tasks. In this study, we conduct an experimental assessment of a force regulation task employing a virtual force sensor based on the perturbation observer proposed by Mohammadi et al. The effectiveness of this approach is validated through a comparison with the performance of an industrial force sensor.

articleTitle: Outer Synchronization and Formation of Two Complex Heterogeneous Robotic Networks with an Intermediary Dynamic System
abstract: This work addresses the study related to the analysis of two terrestrial and aerial robotic networks. The network of terrestrial robots consists of mobile robots of the differential traction type, while the network of aerial robots is made up of robots of the quadcopter type. The inner coupling of the two complex robotic networks is in a directed star type topology, on the other hand, the outer coupling between the two networks is carried out through an intermediary dynamic system that couples the two master nodes of each of the complex robotic networks. To achieve the tracking of desired trajectories in each of the robotic networks innerlly, two control techniques are used, in the case of the terrestrial robotic network a dynamic feedback linearization is used, while in the case of the aerial robotic network a backstepping control is used. To corroborate the proposed network coupling approach, numerical simulations of nine robots in each of the networks programmed in the Matlab software using the Simulink environment are presented, where the results can be extended to <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$M$</tex> networks with <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$N$</tex> nodes.

articleTitle: Neural Networks for the Detection of Distractions in Drivers
abstract: Due to high rates of self-inflicted accidents, driving a car is a demanding activity that requires the driver to prepare both physically and mentally. In this sense, driving assistance systems play an important role in preventing distractions and road accidents. In this work, we detect and classify driver distractions using convolutional neural networks trained first with the “State Farm Distracted Driver Detection” and then with a custom database. Furthermore, with the use of the TensorFlow Lite library, the trained model is deployed on a mobile device for real-time use. The best trained model reaches an accuracy of 91% in training and 95% in validation, thus resulting in a highly discriminating model for each of the classes (distractions) to be classified. In other words, 10 different classes have been identified: one of them is “safe driving” and the other 9 correspond to those most responsible for accidents. With the system's implementation on the mobile device, the test accuracy is reduced to 90% however it correctly detects distractions regardless of the class to which they belong. The initial results demonstrated the possibility of adapting an ADAS in a mobile device to detect distractions and generate real-time audible voice alerts.

articleTitle: Design, Construction and Control of a Seesaw System Driven with a Thrust Propeller
abstract: This work presents the design, instrumentation, and control of a seesaw system powered by a propeller mounted on a DC motor. The system was designed using SolidWorks and fabricated using a 3-D printer. It employs an Arduino Mega as a data acquisition board, establishing a connection with Matlab Simulink. The angular position of the seesaw is measured using a linear resistor(potenciometer), which is characterized using the least squares method. Subsequently, the propeller was mounted onto a DC motor, and the system's transfer function was characterized through the analysis of the step response. For this purpose, the input was the armature voltage of the motor, and the output was the angular position of the seesaw. The electromechanical device's control was performed using a proportional-integral-derivative control designed via the Ziegler-Nichols first and second method.

articleTitle: A Comparative Study of Different Chattering Reduction Techniques for Sliding Mode Controllers
abstract: This paper presents the observation and quantification of the reduction in chattering in the implementation of the sliding mode control technique as a regulator of a pendulum driven by a direct drive motor. Initially, five controllers based on the sign function are developed, and the substitution of this function by the saturation and relay functions, which are responsible for smoothing the response of chattering, is performed to obtain 15 controllers to be analyzed.

articleTitle: Rotation Control About One Axis Using Two V-Gimbaled CMGs
abstract: This work presents a combination of modeling and control techniques for the angle regulation of a rigid body. The proposed scheme includes using quaternions for modeling the rigid body, a feedback linearization scheme that considers the mechanism of torque transmission, and using a robust observer to estimate the angular velocity. This scheme yields good regulation even in the presence of large perturbations.

articleTitle: Implementation of Potential Fields in a Differential Mobile Robot
abstract: This paper presents the implementation of the autonomous navigation technique, Potential Fields. It describes the model of the mobile robot in a differential configuration, considering a point displaced from the axis of action of the wheels. In addition, it discusses the robot's odometry and the implementation of the autonomous navigation method for obstacle avoidance. The study presents results from both simulations in the CoppeliaSim environment and experimental tests on a mobile robot in a differential configuration. This robot was built using low-cost electronics such as the ESP32 development board and 6 HCSR-04 ultrasonic sensors. This provides a valuable opportunity to learn and acquire practical knowledge about mobile robotics and the implementation of navigation and control algorithms.

articleTitle: Tuning of a State Feedback Controller Using MOPSO
abstract: This work deals with the tuning of state feedback controllers by means of the Multi-Objective Particle Swarm Optimization (MOPSO) algorithm, which simultaneously optimizes several complex fitness functions in the Pareto optimal sense. Classical techniques for controller tuning may not be able to handle these complex fitness functions, excepting in some particular cases as the Linear Quadratic Regulator methodology, which minimizes quadratic functions of the state and the control signal. This work employs the MOPSO algorithm using two conflicting fitness functions. One depends on the tracking error, while the other considers the variation and the amplitude of the controller signal. The outcomes are validated using numerical simulations of a servo system as a case study. These results allow observing the effects of the tuning on the closed-loop response according to the weights provided for each fitness function.

articleTitle: Control of an Underactuated Mobile Robot Using the Path-Following Technique
abstract: Research in motion control for autonomous mobile robots has increased in recent decades. In this sense, fully actuated robots have been extensively studied to control their position, perform trajectory tracking, control the force/torque of the robot, or a combination of these. However, applying these control strategies to underactuated systems remains an active research topic. This paper deals with the motion control of an underactuated sixth-order system, which, given its nature, has an internal dynamic that can cause the system not to converge to the desired values. To solve this problem, the path-following approach is proposed so that the internal dynamics are bounded and the system states converge to the desired value. The results are presented through numerical simulations considering that the system follows a straight line at a certain angle. In addition, a comparison of the behavior of the internal dynamics is made when applying and not applying the path-following technique.

articleTitle: Modeling. Parameterization, and State Feedback Control of a Furuta Pendulum
abstract: This article presents a Furuta pendulum as a test bed to experimentally validate a state feedback control with input constraints, which is designed with basis on the quadratic Lyapunov function. The mathematical model of the Furuta pendulum is derived using the Euler-Lagrange formulation. Unknown parameters are estimated using data obtained from open-loop experiments. The system is linearized for controller design, and Linear Matrix Inequalities (LMIs) are developed to compute the gains, considering an input voltage constraint of up to 12 V.

articleTitle: Implementation in an Electronic Development Board of a Hybrid Computational Learning System for the Optimization of Artificial Neural Networks for Autonomous Mobile Robots
abstract: Artificial Neural Networks (ANN) used to control autonomous robots must be trained to guarantee their proper functioning. In most cases, unsupervised computational algorithms are used to optimize neural networks in simulators, which regularly generates discrepancies at the end of the process between virtual and real environments (reality gap). As for the learning processes developed in real environments, they are typically slow, reaching several days to obtain satisfactory results. Therefore, an option based on real environments is presented which uses a hybrid approach in an obstacle avoidance task. An ANN is trained using supervised learning and a database containing some of the environmental stimuli. Afterwards, a generational genetic algorithm is created for the optimization of ANN, including the previously trained network as an initial individual. This algorithm is housed in an electronic development board to control a differential robot, which has ultrasonic and infrared sensors for collision detection. The performance of supervised, unsupervised and hybrid learning is compared with the same robotic platform, which demonstrates a better aptitude value for the created alternative. Thus, the hybrid learning system allows reducing unsupervised training time in real environments using a microcontroller with limited memory capacities. This offers an alternative for learning autonomous robots with different locomotion mechanisms and electronic components.

articleTitle: Measurement of Water Quality Using an Unmanned Surface Vehicle
abstract: In order to ensure the quality of water, required for its different applications, it is necessary to design monitoring instruments that allow safety measures to be taken as soon as possible. This project proposes the design and construction of an unmanned surface vehicle equipped with a water quality measurement module that can be used to evaluate rivers, lakes, dams, etc. This paper shows the analysis of the different variables that determine the quality of a body of water and defines 4 parameters that can be evaluated in situ, temperature, pH, turbidity, total dissolved solids. The proposed system has the capacity to gather the data of the selected parameters which can be used to provide a preliminary diagnosis in situ, in addition the system associates the measurements with GPS coordinates to provide a spatial information of the exploration area. Finally, experimental tests are also presented in a spring located in the state of Hidalgo, Mexico.

articleTitle: Experimental Validation of an Attitude Controller for a Quadcopter by Means of a Test Bench
abstract: This paper presents different parametrizations to describe the orientation of rigid bodies. In particular, we focus on the exponential coordinates of rotation. In this regard, a control law based on this three-parameter parametrization is proposed to stabilize the rigid body's attitude. The main objective of this study is to assess the performance of the orientation controller experimentally. In that sense, a test bench for small quadcopters and satellites was design, which its structure also works as an educational tool. The mechanism allows to perform full 360-degree rotations around the three axes, and provides precise angle measurements. In order to assess the test bench, a custom quadcopter was designed and implemented from scratch.

articleTitle: Trajectory Tracking and Obstacle Avoidance with Turtlebot 3 Burger and ROS 2
abstract: The paper presents the implementation of trajectory tracking and obstacle avoidance algorithms on a Turtlebot 3 Burger using the ROS 2 operating system. A proportional control with compensation is used for lemniscate and circle trajectory tracking. In addition, an potential artificial field (APF) algorithm is incorporated for obstacle avoidance in dynamic environments. In this approach, the robot is modeled as a particle immersed in a potential field that uses attractive functions to reach a destination point and repulsive functions to go around obstacles. Simulated tests in Gazebo software and experimental tests are performed to validate the performance of the algorithms. The results showed that the route followed meets the requirements of the problem, confirming that the proposed route planning approach is efficient.
